messages:
ian: seeing ALB target deregistration across edge pool in eu-west-1 since 13:04 UTC. A bunch of targets marked unhealthy and removed. health checks are timing out (504) even though app reports ready locally.

maya: which LB? ALB or NLB? any recent deploys?

ian: ALB (ip target group). No deploys in last hour per deploy-bot. Here's the ALB logs for one target:
```
2026-02-28T13:04:02.123Z ALB: \"Target response failed: 504 Gateway Timeout\" target=10.0.65.12:8080
2026-02-28T13:04:05.456Z Target deregistered: reason=\"unhealthy\" code=504
```

raj: do kube readiness probes look healthy? sometimes readiness probe timeout < ALB healthcheck so ALB thinks pod is down

ian: readinessProbe configured: periodSeconds:10 timeoutSeconds:1 successThreshold:1 failureThreshold:3. Pod logs show readiness endpoint returning 200 but taking 2-3s during model hot reloads. So readiness probe times out.

kyle: ah that explains it — probe timeout is too aggressive. ALB health check interval is 10s with 2s timeout and unhealthy threshold 3 -> after ~30s it deregisters

maya: but why is readiness slow? model loads only on GPU warmup. Were there evictions or OOMs?

ian: metric spike on GPU memory and CPU during that window. Several pods hit high CPU while loading weights. Not OOM, just blocking on OpenMM load. We also saw SNAT exhaustion warnings on nodes right before health checks started failing.

ops-bot: node/node-45: SNAT ports exhausted (count=65535) — ephemeral port reuse high

raj: if nodes ran out of SNAT ports ALB health checks that require outbound calls (if check uses Host header with resolver) might be impacted. But ALB health checks are inbound to pod IP. SNAT shouldn't matter unless readiness probe calls external service.

ian: readiness endpoint calls a small internal probe that queries model-serving process over localhost. No external calls. SNAT may be separate symptom from high connection churn.

kyle: mitigation options (short term):
- increase readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds to 5
- set initialDelaySeconds to 30 for new replicas
- increase ALB target group healthcheck timeout to 5s and unhealthy threshold to 5
- enable deregistration delay / connection draining

maya: long term: make readiness not block on model load (return ready=false quickly until warm) or asynchronous warmup with graceful readiness after warm.

ian: patch I'm testing now:
```
kubectl patch deployment edge-model --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/timeoutSeconds","value":5}]'
```

deploy-bot: no active rollouts in last 60m

ian: after patching readiness timeout and ALB TG timeout increase, targets are staying healthy. 95th latency from ALB->pod dropped back under 200ms. Will follow up with a PR to change defaults for model-serving deployments.

maya: please open a postmortem with root cause: aggressive probe + model warmups + SNAT port exhaustion (if confirmed). Also add runbook steps: change probe timeouts and TG settings per service.

raj: also add a check to cluster autoscaler to avoid mass pod restarts on node pressure leading to warmups at once.

kyle: note to infra: consider enabling per-node SNAT port pool or use NAT gateway with enhanced mapping to avoid port exhaustion on high p2p connection scenarios.

ian: ack. I'll write up notes and send incident summary. Thanks all :thumbsup:
